title: Collages of coherent space-valued bimodules
statement:
Use quasicategories, spaces, coherent functors and transformations in fixed nested universes as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $C,D$ be small infinity-categories and $H:C^{\mathrm{op}}\times D\to\mathrm{Spc}$ a small-space-valued coherent functor. There exists a small infinity-category $\operatorname{Coll}(H)\to[1]$ with full endpoint fibers $C,D$, having mixed mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Coll}(H)}(c,d)\simeq H(c,d)$ and empty mapping spaces from $D$ to $C$. The mixed precomposition and postcomposition maps, including all higher compatibilities, are exactly the two functorial actions of $H$.

This collage admits the following coherent string presentation. Its objects are the disjoint endpoint objects; composable strings have nondecreasing endpoint labels. A string wholly in one endpoint has that endpoint's data. A mixed string has exactly one change of endpoint, with its crossing labeled by $H$, and the remaining arrows in $C$ and $D$. Faces composing across the change use the actions of $H$; other faces use endpoint composition; degeneracies use endpoint units. Use the complete Segal-space conventions and their comparison with quasicategories of [lem-coef-complete-segal-quasicategory-comparison]. This describes a complete Segal-space presentation, with homotopy fiber products and coherent endpoint object spaces understood. In particular, giving coherent families of mixed arrows, with prescribed endpoint diagrams, means giving their crossing labels and all the action compatibilities of these mixed strings. The construction and identifications can be made coherently in $H$, in endpoint functors, and in additional small simplicial parameters.

source.place: Section 2.3.1, Definition 2.3.1.3 and Remark 2.3.1.4 (printed pp. 96-97), correspondences and functors C^op x D to spaces. The explicit complete-Segal string presentation and parameter bookkeeping are agent-formulated refinements of that correspondence, not a quotation of a numbered theorem. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag supplies it.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-strict-bimodule-rectification] to $H$; it uses the Bergner model structure and coherent-nerve comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] and the space and universe conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. It supplies Bergner cofibrant, locally Kan simplicial categories $A,B$ with equivalences $N_{\mathrm{hc}}A\simeq C$, $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B\simeq D$, a strict simplicial functor $M:A^{\mathrm{op}}\times B\to\mathsf{sSet}$ with $\mathcal U$-small Kan values, an equivalence of its coherent nerve with the transported $H$, and strict commuting $A$- and $B$-actions corresponding to the two actions of $H$. The equivalence preserves the identity and composition simplices and is natural in $H$, endpoint functors, and small parameters, so no one-variable presheaf rectification or strict equality of a Segal-space composite is being assumed.

source.place: §2.2.1 and §2.2.5, with Appendix A.3.3; strict two-variable consequence stated in lem-coef-strict-bimodule-rectification

proof.text: On the disjoint object set $\operatorname{Ob}(A)\amalg\operatorname{Ob}(B)$, form the strict simplicial category $\mathcal K$ with diagonal enriched categories $A$ and $B$, reverse mapping simplicial sets $\mathcal K(b,a)=\varnothing$, and mixed mapping simplicial sets $\mathcal K(a,b)=M(a,b)$. The identity vertices are those of $A$ and $B$. For $a\in A$, $b\in B$, composition $\mathcal K(b,b')\times\mathcal K(a,b)\to\mathcal K(a,b')$ is the covariant $B$-action of $M$ and $\mathcal K(a,b)\times\mathcal K(a',a)\to\mathcal K(a',b)$ is its contravariant $A$-action; a composite with two endpoint arrows uses the two commuting actions, and the associativity and unit equations for composable triples (any triple through a reverse hom is vacuous) are exactly the enriched-functor equations for $M$. Thus $\mathcal K$ is a well-defined directed strict collage, and its mixed mapping simplicial sets are Kan.

source.place: §2.3.1, Definition 2.3.1.3 and Remark 2.3.1.4; the strict enriched construction is written out here

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-triangular-cofibrant-resolution] to $\mathcal K$ with $U=\operatorname{Ob}A$, $V=\operatorname{Ob}B$ and the endpoint identity resolutions $A\to A$, $B\to B$, which are local trivial fibrations fixing objects with Bergner cofibrant sources (Step 1). It gives a Bergner-cofibrant strict triangular collage $\widetilde{\mathcal K}$ with the same two endpoint blocks, empty reverse mapping sets, projectively cofibrant mixed bimodule $N$, and a local trivial fibration $\widetilde{\mathcal K}\to\mathcal K$ that is the identity on objects and endpoint blocks. Since $\mathcal K(a,b)=M(a,b)$ is Kan and $N(a,b)\to M(a,b)$ is a trivial Kan fibration, each $N(a,b)$ is Kan and $N(a,b)\to M(a,b)$ is a weak equivalence. The endpoint models are locally Kan, the mixed $N(a,b)$ are Kan and the reverse sets are empty, so $\widetilde{\mathcal K}$ is locally Kan. The construction is functorial for maps of the endpoint models and of the bimodule.

source.place: Appendix A.3.3, Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5, specialized to the two endpoint blocks

proof.text: The coherent nerve $\operatorname{Coll}(H)=N_{\mathrm{hc}}\widetilde{\mathcal K}$ is a small infinity-category by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The simplicial functor $\widetilde{\mathcal K}\to[1]$ sending $A$ to $0$ and $B$ to $1$ is defined because reverse mapping sets are empty; its coherent nerve is the projection $\operatorname{Coll}(H)\to\Delta^1$, the coherent nerve of the discrete category $[1]$ being its ordinary nerve. The fiber over $0$ (resp. $1$) consists of the simplices whose vertices lie in $A$ (resp. $B$), i.e. $N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$ (resp. $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B$) since these are full subcategories, and hence identifies with $C$ (resp. $D$) through the chosen equivalences. The mapping-space comparison in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], which preserves enriched composition with its coherent homotopies, together with $N(a,b)\simeq M(a,b)\simeq H(a,b)$, gives the mixed mapping-space equivalence compatibly with the two actions, while the reverse mapping space is $\widetilde{\mathcal K}(b,a)=\varnothing$.

An $n$-simplex of $N_{\mathrm{hc}}\widetilde{\mathcal K}$ is an enriched functor $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to\widetilde{\mathcal K}$. Because $\widetilde{\mathcal K}$ has no $B$-to-$A$ mapping simplices, its object labels are nondecreasing and a mixed simplex has exactly one change from $A$ to $B$; its crossing edge is a vertex of $N(a,b)$, all other edges are endpoint arrows, and the higher subset-poset simplices spanning the change land in the mixed sets $N(-,-)$. Enriched composition gives the cross-change faces and endpoint composition gives the remaining faces; degeneracies insert endpoint identities. The coherent nerve therefore has exactly the asserted one-crossing string presentation and all its higher action compatibilities. Applying the natural equivalence $R:\mathrm{Cat}_\infty\simeq\mathrm{CSS}_\infty$ of [lem-coef-complete-segal-quasicategory-comparison] supplies the complete Segal-space presentation, its mapping fibers being the mapping spaces of Step 4, and preserves equivalences and naturality in $H$, endpoint functors, and small parameters.

source.place: §2.3.1, Definition 2.3.1.3 and Remark 2.3.1.4; complete-Segal comparison of §2.2.5
